data.reason: Both readings name the same crux in different words: the worm/cure must stay undecidably disease, fortune, and Liu himself through three equally-weighted closing answers and an explicit refusal to choose, and that suspension depends on holding the dry, learned strange-tale telling against section three's prolonged bodily torment. Option 1 states that second point more usefully for translation, as a performed pastiche voice rather than only a contrast of weathers, with its evidence tied to the text.
data.say:
Pick: Option 1, from the crux check (Wonder). This is the same crux as Option 0, not a competing one: an undecidable worm whose expulsion is both perfect cure and ruin, left unresolved by three parallel explanations, and a cool, borrowed tale-telling set against one passage of bodily suffering. Option 1 goes forward because it names the frame as pastiche — the performed Chinese strange tale — which gives the English a clearer rule for diction and register without settling the story's meaning.

House log: The two independent crux readings were judged the same; Option 1 was adopted as written.
